system_label: Arm B1: one agent with generic evidence tools only (no checks)

findings.rationale: Shell history under account jpark shows clinic-export of dataset patients_full written to a hidden /tmp path (about 20.6 MB per fs_stat). Staging a full patient dataset outside the records system is a precursor to bulk transfer.
verifier_notes: an object of matching size was written on this host shortly before a non-approved bulk transfer

findings.rationale: Shell history shows curl upload of the staged /tmp/.font-unix/idx-3e08.bin to 10.20.9.87:8080. The tap flow record independently shows 20,582,305 bytes sent from 10.20.1.21 (the workstation address seen in records access logs) to that destination. This is above the 5,000,000-byte bulk threshold and the destination is not an approved bulk destination (stor-nas-01 10.20.0.45, lab-gw-01 10.20.8.20), so it violates transfer policy.
verifier_notes: bulk transfer to a destination not on the approved list, cited via the flow record

findings.rationale: Repeated small curl uploads of single lab request PDFs (roughly 340-750 KB each) from tmori and jpark to lab-gw-01 (10.20.8.20), an approved destination for laboratory and registry submissions, and below the bulk threshold. Policy-consistent.
verifier_notes: references resolve; no allegation is made

findings.rationale: A roughly 20.6 MB transfer to stor-nas-01 (approved backup and log archive) at 11:59, launched by the svc-backup scheduled backup-incremental cron job. Destination is approved; consistent with routine backup.
verifier_notes: a deterministic check supports this observation; it is not an incident allegation

limits: No evidence ties a specific person to the session.
Shared console credentials; badge readers can miss tailgating.
Remote VPN sessions are not covered by badge records.
attribution.statement: Account jpark was used at the workstation (ws-nurse-01) for the staging and upload of a patient dataset export. Human operator not established. The account is a credential, and console credentials at the shared station have been found written down before. The jpark tty1 session (workstation#74) was open 11:14:18 to 11:20:41 UTC. Badge B-2333 (account jpark's listed badge) was recorded in at 08:03 and out at 11:57, so the badge places that credential's holder in the building during the window, but badge data cannot establish who used the console.

summary: Records access and transfers this shift. Supported incident finding: at 11:15 UTC, account jpark on workstation ws-nurse-01 ran clinic-export of the patients_full dataset to a hidden path (/tmp/.font-unix/idx-3e08.bin, ~20.6 MB). At 11:18:27 the same session uploaded that file via curl to 10.20.9.87:8080. The tap flow shows 20.58 MB sent to that destination, above the 5 MB bulk threshold and not an approved destination. This violates transfer policy. Benign or consistent activity: small lab-request uploads to the approved lab-gw-01 (10.20.8.20); a 20.6 MB backup to approved stor-nas-01 (10.20.0.45) by the svc-backup cron job; records access.log rotation that archived the file off-host by design. No log removal was found: the collector copies match host logs for the records auth log and the workstation auth log. Attribution: account jpark was used; the human operator is not established. Remote VPN and shared console credentials are possible.
open_questions: Who holds or used the jpark credential at 11:14-11:20 UTC, and was the console session shared?
What is the destination 10.20.9.87:8080, and was it authorized?
The workstation auth.log.1 generation was not examined in detail; the collector copies align with the host logs for the windows checked.
Metadata snapshots and shell histories are host-local and not forwarded; their completeness cannot be independently verified.
